newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's 91-day T-bill rates, volumes higher.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's 91-day T-bill rates, volumes higher.

text.p: Kenya's main 91-day category of treasury bills were seen higher on Thursday and as the Central Bank of Kenya accepted bigger volumes of bids in an effort to reduce liquidity in the market, a bank official said on Friday.
The central bank said it accepted all bids tendered worth 11.353 billion shillings, which was above the 10 billion it had invited last week.
"Normally the redemptions for the week are used as a guideline, but this week we were also targetting reserve monies," a central bank official said.
The bank expects some 10.4 billion shillings worth of redemptions this week.

In the 28-day category, the bank said it accepted bids at an average yield of 16.384 percent from 16.500 percent, while on the 91-day category, it accepted bids at an average yield of 21.633 percent from 21.604 percent.
Some 11.333 billion shillings were accepted for the 91-day treasury bill while 15.85 million shillings were accepted for the 28-day treasury bill.
In the 182-day category of bills the bank accepted four million shillings of bids at an average yield of 19.999 percent.
The bank invited tenders for treasury bills eight billion for next week's Thursday auction.
